 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor
Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.14,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic
accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 06-09-2022 at about 11.00 p.m., the Petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing No.KA-04-JA-5138 near Sub-Register office, 14th Cross, Peenya 2nd stage, Bengaluru, at that time, all of a sudden a motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-EF-4887 ridden by its rider in rash and negligent manner with high speed and overtook his motor cycle and without any indication suddenly turned into right direction and dashed the motor cycle.
Due to the impact, the petitioner and rider were thrown out, fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was admitted to Sri Lakshmi Multi Speciality hospital, Magadi main road, Bengaluru from 08.09.2022 to 12.09.2022.
He has spent Rs.50,000/- towards medical treatment, conveyance and the incidental expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working in a private company and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.
4. The Respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of motor cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. Despite of service of notice, the Respondent No.2 remained absent, as such he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 appeared before the court through its counsel and filed objections to the main petition.

6. Respondent No.1 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motor cycle.

Further it contended that the offending motor cycle was not at all involved in Udaya Kumar H.B vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12858384/
2 the accident.

sentences.text: Further contended that the motor cycle was not insured by them.

The rider of the alleged motor cycle had no valid driving licence to ride the motor cycle and the owner has consciously permitted a non licencee to drive the vehicle in flagrant violation of the express terms of the policy statute Section 3 and 5 of MV Act.
On these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
7. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 06-09- 2022 at about 11.00 p.m. near Sub-Register Office, 14th Cross, Peenya 2nd Stage, Bengaluru City due to rash and negligent riding of rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-EF-4887?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?

3. What Order or Award?
8.
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.14 and closed his side evidence.

On the other hand,
Respondent No.1 examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and closed its side evidence.

9. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1 and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 10. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 06-09-2022 at about 11.00 p.m. due to the rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-EF-4887 by its rider.
11. On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing Regn. No.KA-02-EF-4887 by its rider.
12. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-14.
He has re-iterated the Petition averments in his chief-affidavit.

sentences.text: Ex.P-1 is the certified copy of FIR, Ex.P.2 is the certified copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 is the certified copy of spot mahazar along with sketch, Ex.P.4 is the certified copy of notice issued u/s 133 of MV Act, Ex,P,5 is the reply given to notice.

Ex.P.6 is the certified copy of IMV report, Ex.P.7 is the certified copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is the certified copy of charge sheet, Ex.P.9 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.10 is the medical bills.
Ex.P.11 is IPD receipt, Ex.P.12 is prescriptions.
Ex.P.13 is the notarized copy of aadhar card of petitioner and Ex.P.14 is medical bills.

13. Upon going through Ex.P.1 & 2 FIR and Complaint, they justify the fact that on the complaint lodged before Peenya Traffic Police Station, the concerned Police have registered the case against the rider of motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-02- EF-4887 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Ex. P.3 is the Spot mahazar along with sketch, which shows that mahazar was drawn and sketch was prepared in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.6 is the IMV report, which shows that accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects and also justify the fact of involvement of vehicle in question in the accident.
The Ex.P.7 is the wound certificate, which shows that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

The Ex.P.8 Charge sheet shows that after thorough investigation,
the Peenya Traffic Police have Charge-sheeted the rider of the offending motor cycle for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
14.
Further respondent No.1 has examined its Manager Legal as RW.1.
In the cross examination nothing is elicited to disbelieve the contentions of petitioner.

15. Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
But there is no evidence to show that the said injuries are in the nature of permanent disablement.
In order to prove the permanent disablement the petitioner has not examined any doctor and not produced assessment report.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Partly Affirmative'.
16. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending motor cycle by its rider, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17.
In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 48 years.
He has produced Aadhar card at Ex.P.13 to prove his age.
As per Aadhar card, his date of birth is shown as 19.07.1974.
The accident took place on 06.09.2022.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident was taken as 48 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
18. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working in a private company and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.15,500/-p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2022, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.

sentences.text: With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.
It is to be noted here that according to the petitioner, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.7 wound certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries.

1. Swelling of left knee with painful movements, underlying ligamental injuries (ACL, MCl and medial and lateral miniscus tear (MRI left knee No.N491621)
2. Abrasion measuring 4 cm x 2cm present over left elbow.
Wherein the doctor has opined that injury No.1 is grievous and injury No.2 is simple in nature.
20. In order to prove the gravity of the injuries, the Petitioner is expected to produce documents.
The petitioner has deposed that he incurred expenditure of Rs.50,000/- for his treatment and other expenses.
In this regard he has produced medical Bills at Ex.P.10 amounting to Rs.58,628/- and Ex.P.14 amounting to Rs.32,832/- totally amounting to Rs.91,460/-.
As there is no serious dispute with regard to the medical bills and upon careful consideration, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.91,460/-towards medical expenses.
21. It is the case of the Petitioner that he has suffered permanent disability.

However, petitioner has not examined any doctor and in the absence of physical disability and considering the nature of injury sustained by the Petitioner and the medical expenses incurred for the treatment.
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, he was admitted on 07.09.2022 and discharged on 12.09.2022.

Keeping in mind all these factors and the expenses incurred for Food and other charges, this Tribunal is of the opinion that awarding global compensation including medical bill amount of Rs.1,50,000/-
would be just and proper.

22. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-EF-4887.
Further, though the Respondent No.1 in its written statement denied the issuance of policy, the RW.1 in his examination in chief no single word is stated about validity or invalidity of policy.
Therefore it is considered as there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle as on the date of accident.
Therefore, Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 being the owner are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
23. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
